adjudicated_statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients. Let S be a reduced separated finite-type C-scheme, let Delta_0 subset P^2 be a closed subscheme of dimension at most 1, and set U_0=P^2 minus Delta_0. For a product (equivalently, constant (CE)+(N)+(BAL)) family with U isomorphic to S times U_0, compact-support Kunneth of mixed Hodge structures and the projective-bundle formula identify Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(S times P^2;Q) with the direct sum of three pure weight-16 summands Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(S;Q) direct-sum Gr^W_14 H_c^{14}(S;Q)(-1) direct-sum Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(S;Q)(-2), corresponding to fibre degrees 2j for j=0,1,2. Compact-support localization along U_0 subset P^2 is a long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures; at the weight-equals-degree corner Gr^W is exact, so the fibre-degree-2j projective-bundle summand of A=S times P^2 lies in the image of Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U;Q) if and only if the restriction Gr^W_{2j} H_c^{2j}(P^2;Q) -> Gr^W_{2j} H_c^{2j}(Delta_0;Q) vanishes. Vanishing of H_c^{2j}(Delta_0;Q) is sufficient for that restriction to vanish, and holds whenever 2j>2 dim Delta_0. Thus the fibre-degree-2 summand Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(S;Q)(-2) always survives in such product families as a direct Kunneth summand of Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U;Q), equivalently H_c^4(U_0;Q)=Q(-2), because H_c^4 of a curve vanishes; this is the class used by ATT-0119. If Delta_0 is nonempty and proper then H_c^0(U_0;Q)=0, so the fibre-degree-0 summand Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(S;Q) does not appear in H_c^{16}(U;Q); the restriction H_c^2(P^2)->H_c^2(Delta_0) is typically nonzero for a positive-degree plane curve, so the fibre-degree-1 projective-bundle summand need not arise from U. Independently, on a non-product FND-0167 family with S of pure dimension 15, the discriminant Delta subset A has dimension 16, so Deligne's Hodge-number bound (Theorie de Hodge III, Theorem 8.2.4(ii)) does not force F^{15} H_c^{16}(Delta;C)=0. This is why FND-0171 blocks transporting the (H-S) j=8 / fibre-degree-0 first summand of ATT-0118 to U, while it does not block the ATT-0119 fibre-fundamental-class class, which is already a Kunneth summand of H_c^{16}(U) itself. The FND-0167 corner map injects Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U) into the three summands and cannot by itself transport non-Tateness from any ambient summand to U; survival of the third summand in product families is a kernel/Kunneth statement, not a reverse of that injection. Fibrewise restriction on Delta_0 does not by itself control non-product families at fibre degrees j=0,1 without a compact-support Leray argument, which FND-0164 withholds for nonconstant coefficients. No assertion is made about RED-0001, about T_16 of a dimension-17 model over a dimension-15 atlas of Hbar^bal, or about S_6-isotypics other than the S_6-invariants of the product model.
contradiction_resolution: Mandatory first reads of ATT-0119 and REV-0167 confirm the contested passage. ATT-0119 section 4 identifies H_c^4(U_0;Q)=Q(-2) by Poincare duality on a smooth connected surface and independently by compact-support localization of U_0 subset P^2 against a proper plane curve Delta_0 of dimension 1 (H_c^3(Delta_0)=H_c^4(Delta_0)=0). Section 5 realises Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(S;Q) tensor Q(-2) as a Kunneth summand of Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U;Q) for the product U=S x U_0. Section 6 states that this is the third FND-0167 summand, not a lift of Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(S), and that H_c^4(P^2)->H_c^4(Delta_0) vanishes because dim Delta_0=1. REV-0167 confirms CLM-0119-4, CLM-0119-5, and CLM-0119-6, and strongest-attack (ii) records that an initial suspicion that H_c^4 of the discriminant curve might be nonzero confused it with H_c^2. Packet FND-0167 supplies the corner injection Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U) into Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(S) + Gr^W_14 H_c^{14}(S)(-1) + Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(S)(-2) and does not assert surjectivity. Packet FND-0171 records that this injection cannot transport non-Tateness from S to U and that, on a pure-dimension-15 base, dim Delta=16 so Deligne's F^{15} vanishing used for dimension-at-most-14 complements fails; it leaves Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U) and Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(Z) open. No contradiction with CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001 (contradicts_claim_ids empty). Distinct from FND-0171: that finding blocks the fibre-degree-0 / (H-S) j=8 first summand on dimension-15 bases; the present finding supplies the complementary product-family survival of the fibre-degree-2 third summand. Do not merge. Primary checks: Deligne, Theorie de Hodge III, Theorem 8.2.4, states that nonzero Hodge numbers h^{p,q} of H^n(X) satisfy (i) p,q>=0 and (ii) if dim X=N then (p,q) lies in [n-N,N] x [n-N,N], hence F^p vanishes for p>dim X; (iii) proper implies p+q<=n; (iv) smooth implies p+q>=n. Proposition 8.2.10 gives Kunneth as mixed Hodge structures for ordinary cohomology of products of separated finite-type C-schemes, and Corollary 8.2.8 / Wikipedia Mixed Hodge structure records the compact-support localization sequence H_c^m(U)->H^m(X)->H^m(Y). Topological cohomological dimension gives H_c^k(X;Q)=0 for k>2 dim_C X, so H_c^4 of a curve vanishes. Stacks tag 0FMG Lemma 50.11.4 gives H^{2i}_{dR}(P^n)=A c_1(O(1))^i for 0<=i<=n and zero otherwise, matching H_c^{2j}(P^2)=Q(-j) for j=0,1,2. The original candidate overstated two points, which the adjudicated statement corrects: (1) fibrewise restriction H_c^{2j}(P^2)->H_c^{2j}(Delta_0) rigorously controls the three FND-0167 summands only for product families via Kunneth, not for general relative P^2-bundles without a Leray argument withheld by FND-0164; (2) vanishing of H_c^{2j}(Delta_0) is sufficient for the restriction to vanish and, among fibre degrees j=0,1,2 with dim Delta_0<=1, is equivalent to 2j>2 dim Delta_0, but is not a general iff. The 16-dimensional discriminant clause is the non-product dim-S=15 geometry of FND-0171, not the product-family fibrewise picture. With those hypotheses restored, the explanation of why FND-0171 blocks ATT-0118 but not ATT-0119 is correct.
